gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Audio-Technica AT-LP70X's built-in preamp puts out 252 mV at LINE, about 18 dB below a 2 V line input, or that this is about 5 dB hotter than the Fluance RT81's 140 mV. Through the same powered speakers, the AT plays about 5 dB louder at the same volume setting.
standout_why: I read four of the result pages. fewbetter.com's turntable page has no turntable content at all. valveandvinyl.com/turntables/crosley-alternatives gives Audio-Technica's 36 dB nominal preamp gain for the AT-LP70X, AT-LP60XBT and AT-LP120XUSB, but no output voltage for any deck. platterandplinth.com/turntables/best-with-preamp gives the Sony PS-LX3BT's gain steps (−4/0/+6 dB) but no mV figures. stylusandsound.com/best-turntables-with-built-in-preamp/ gives the Fluance RT81+ as 4.0 mV phono and 140 mV line, so the Fluance side of the comparison is already published. None of them gives the AT-LP70X's 252 mV line output, its distance from 2 V, or the 5 dB gap between the two picks. Half the inputs are on rival pages, so the score is 1, not 2.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's beginner pick. The AT-LP70X has the hotter built-in preamp, which matters most with low-sensitivity powered speakers or a soundbar AUX input. The RT81 sits about 23 dB below 2 V, so it needs the volume turned up further. A 5 dB gap is a loudness difference, not a sound-quality verdict, so it doesn't reverse the RT81 pick for buyers who want manual control.

findings.label: Built-in preamp LINE output level
findings.source_title: Elusive Disc: Audio-Technica AT-LP70X Fully Automatic Belt-Drive Turntable (spec table)
findings.note: This is a retailer's copy of Audio-Technica's spec sheet. Every audio-technica.com page I tried (en-us, en-ca, en-au) returned 403. Same table: PHONO 4.0 mV nominal; preamp gain '36 dB nominal, RIAA equalized'; S/N > 55 dB; W&F < 0.25% (WTD); non-removable AT-VM95C cartridge, VM95C replacement stylus. Check: 252 / 4.0 = 63×, and 20·log10(63) = 36.0 dB, which matches the stated gain.
